title: Ecma International-relevant MDN issues
description: Issue filed on MDN Web Docs related to pages attached to technologies developed by Ecma International

items.content_html:
MDN URL

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Security/Practical_implementation_guides/CORP

What specific section or headline is this issue about?

Examples

What information was incorrect, unhelpful, or incomplete?

I believe SharedArrayBuffer is enabled by COOP + COEP, not CORP and CORP only affects resources, not the enabling of SharedArrayBuffer itself.

Affected text:

Instruct browsers to allow cross-origin resource access, including access to features with unthrottled timers (such as SharedArrayBuffer objects or Performance.now()):

Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin
Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp

This also permits such resources to be embedded.

What did you expect to see?

To enable SharedArrayBuffer and performance.now(), the document must be cross-origin isolated environment. Include the following headers on the document:

Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin
Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp

A page using Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp may only load resources that explicitly allow being embedded.
Resources can opt in using either:

Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy (CORP):

Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: cross-origin

or CORS:

Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://example.com

CORP and CORS do not themselves enable SharedArrayBuffer they only allow resources to be loaded under COEP so that isolation is maintained.

Do you have any supporting links, references, or citations?

No response

Do you have anything more you want to share?

Please suggest if there any improvements are needed to the proposed text, if everything looks good, I would be happy to open a pull to update the documentation.
items.title: [hr-time-3, ecmascript] Fix: CORP does not enable SharedArrayBuffer

items.content_html:
Proposal

I was looking for information on "deep equal" comparison of values in JavaScript, in particular arrays and objects.

Searching MDN, I found related topics in the glossary, such as: Truthy, Falsey, Deep Copy, Shallow Copy. And the Strict equality operator in JavaScript Reference. But no page specifically discussing deep equality.

It seems like a useful topic to add, so I thought I'd suggest it.

The page would probably be suitable for MDN Web Docs Glossary: Definitions of Web-related terms.
